Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. Initial exit polls in Israel's election suggest most
Israelis have voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but the center-right
opposition may struggle to build a governing coalition. Here's NPR's Daniel Estrin.
Exit polls have found Gadi Isenkot, the former military chief, in the lead with his center-right
opposition bloc slightly ahead of Netanyahu's group of far-right ultra-religious parties.
Isenkot's supporters cheered as exit polls were announced.
But votes will continue to be counted and the electoral map could shift.

Isenkot party activist Ofili Namayash.
I'm anxious. Listen, the results are good, but they're complex. It takes time before we have

history and turnout has been the highest in decades. Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
A week out from Election Day in the U.S., the latest NPR/PBS News Marist poll
shows Democrats lead Republicans by eight points on the generic congressional ballot,
NPR's Alina Moore reports.
Democrat Chris Agen in Texas says he never saw himself as an impassioned midterm voter,
but that's changed.
This year is different. This year, it feels like every opportunity to vote is a referendum
against the party in power.
It comes as Democrats nationwide have an enthusiasm advantage, with 71 percent of Democratic likely
voters saying they're very enthusiastic about voting compared to 61 percent of Republicans.
President Trump's low approval may also be a liability for the GOP.
This latest poll finds that 44 percent of likely voters see casting a ballot this year
as a vote against Trump. Alina Moore, NPR News, Washington.
The U.S. has not yet recognized the results of elections in Brazil this week,
but it is welcoming the man who lost a right-wing Trump ally, Flavio Bolsonaro,
as NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports.
The State Department says it will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them
entry into the United States. Bolsonaro lost a run-off election to his left-wing rival,
Luis Inacio Lula da Silva.
A day later, a Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered him to hand in his passports
as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering charges Bolsonaro denies.
Like Bolsonaro, President Trump has suggested the vote was rigged,
though neither provided evidence of that.
Bolsonaro's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, remains under house arrest
after being convicted of attempting a coup following his 2022 election loss.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The manhunt for an escaped inmate has shifted from Tennessee to southern Illinois.
Tennessee authorities say Jacob Morley stole a farm truck about two miles from the prison
where he was serving a life sentence and apparently abandoned it in Marion, Illinois,
about 120 miles north of the prison.
Morley was convicted for killing a coworker four years ago.
Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death in women,
now a coalition of leading medical groups,
has released a new framework for doctors to identify risks
to women's heart health starting in childhood.
And Piers Maria Godoy reports.
Throughout their lives, women experience hormonal changes
that influence heart health in ways men don't experience.
The new framework identifies key life stages that offer windows of opportunity
to prevent heart disease and stroke.
For example, pregnancy complications like gestational diabetes can unmask heart risks,
while changes in cholesterol and metabolic health during perimenopause
can also be early signs of cardiovascular risk.
The guidance comes from the American Medical Association,
the American Academy of Pediatrics,
the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists,
and the Society for Maternal Fetal Medicine.
It appears in the Journal of Circulation.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
Stocks in Asia are rallying in Wednesday trading
and head of an interest rate decision by the Federal Reserve.
The Fed is expected to leave interest rates unchanged
when policymakers wrap up their policy meeting Wednesday.
I'm Jael Snyder.
This is NPR News.
